en.title: Count Elements with Both a Smaller and a Greater Element
en.description:
Given an integer array nums, count how many array elements have both a strictly smaller element and a strictly greater element. This is equivalent to counting the positions that satisfy min(nums) < nums[i] < max(nums); when the same value appears at several positions, every qualifying position is counted.

This site's valid input ranges: 1≤n≤100000, −10^9≤nums[i]≤10^9. The original OAMaster snapshot provides no constraints; the ranges above are this site's additions.

Original problem: https://oamaster.com/docs/companies/uber#26-count-elements-with-at-least-one-smaller-and-one-greater-value (upstream snapshot e66f809f4c953bce129f68491726176615db6afc, catalog content fingerprint 9dcb94388ae360e2eb1df31d2eb9fbfef32ce93fcf3764f24c6da369ff23e5a9).
Semantic cross-check: LeetCode 2148 "Count Elements With Strictly Smaller and Greater Elements", https://leetcode.com/problems/count-elements-with-strictly-smaller-and-greater-elements/.
en.input: The first line contains n; the second line contains n integers nums[i].
en.output: Output the number of array positions that satisfy min(nums)<nums[i]<max(nums).
en.explanation: As long as a value is strictly greater than the global minimum and strictly less than the global maximum, it has both a smaller and a greater element. Count all qualifying positions without deduplicating.
hints: First be clear about the difference between array positions and element values.
Compare decimal representations digit by digit as strings, and do not mistake a prefix for an arbitrary substring.
